description.narrative: A cutting-edge program is proposed to support doctoral and early career women researchers in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) from scientifically-lagging countries (SLCs). The programme builds on an existing postgraduate fellowship programme for doctoral students developed by the Organization for Women in Science for the Developing World (OWSD) and supported since 1998 by Sweden's International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida). A complementary strand for early-career women scientists is supported by Canada’s International Development Centre (IDRC). The program builds on the network and enthusiasm of over 7,000 OWSD members, women scientists with postgraduate degrees living and working in developing countries. The goal is a full suite of mechanisms to support women scientists throughout their careers, increase their influence as scientific leaders in their field or institution, and engage them in innovations through partnership with industry. Over nearly 20 years, more than 400 PhD fellowships have been awarded and more than 300 women from least developed countries and sub-Saharan Africa have graduated; there are currently over 200 women completing their fellowships at host institutes throughout the South. With renewed Sida funding, OWSD will support an additional 140 women from SLCs to obtain PhDs. Many OWSD alumnae are now lecturers and principle investigators in their home institutions but they still face many challenges. With IDRC funding, OWSD will target Early Career women employed at their home institutes in the South and provide the individual and institutional support they need to become influential leaders and decision makers, and make sustainable links with industry and the private sector. The full programme has been designed to allow growth over time. Other donors may wish to expand existing strands or create new ones (mentoring, national chapter support, regional networking, professorial chairs, industry-to-academia fellowships, discipline-based groups). The Elsevier Foundation already funds a highly successful awards scheme run by OWSD to annually reward 5 young researchers from 5 world regions.

Ett spjutspetsprogram föreslås för att stödja kvinnliga forskare på doktorsnivå och tidiga karriärer inom vetenskap, teknik, ingenjörsvetenskap och matematik (STEM) från länder som släpar efter i vetenskapligt hänseende (SLC). Programmet bygger på ett befintligt stipendieprogram för doktorander som utvecklats av Organisationen för kvinnor i vetenskap för utvecklingsvärlden (OWSD) och som sedan 1998 stöds av Sida. En kompletterande del för kvinnliga forskare i tidiga karriärer stöds av Kanadas IDRC. Programmen bygger på nätverket och entusiasmen hos över 7 000 OWSD-medlemmar, kvinnliga forskare med doktorsexamen som bor och arbetar i utvecklingsländer. Målet är en komplett uppsättning mekanismer för att stödja kvinnliga forskare under hela deras karriär, öka deras inflytande som vetenskapliga ledare inom sitt område eller institution och engagera dem i innovationer genom partnerskap med industrin. Under nästan 20 år har mer än 400 doktorandstipendier tilldelats och mer än 300 kvinnor från minst utvecklade länder och Afrika söder om Sahara har tagit examen; Det finns för närvarande över 200 kvinnor som fullföljer sina stipendier vid värdinstitut i hela Syden. Med förnyad Sida-finansiering kommer OWSD att stödja ytterligare 140 kvinnor från STLC för att doktorera. Många OWSD-alumner är nu föreläsare och principiella utredare i sina heminstitutioner men de står fortfarande inför många utmaningar. Med IDRC-finansiering kommer OWSD att rikta in sig på kvinnor i tidiga karriärer som är anställda vid deras heminstitut i söder och ge det individuella och institutionella stöd de behöver för att bli inflytelserika ledare och beslutsfattare, och skapa hållbara kontakter med industrin och den privata sektorn. Hela programmet har utformats för att möjliggöra tillväxt över tid. Andra givare kanske vill utöka befintliga delar eller skapa nya (mentorskap, nationellt avdelningsstöd, regionalt nätverkande, professurer, stipendier från industri till akademi, disciplinbaserade grupper). Elsevier Foundation finansierar redan ett mycket framgångsrikt prisprogram som drivs av OWSD för att årligen belöna 5 unga forskare från 5 världsregioner.

OWSDs övergripande mål är att balansera upp deltagande av kvinnor och transformera kvinnors plats och situation inom naturvetenskaplig och teknisk forskning i låginkomstländerna. Det ligger väl i linje med de övergripande målen för Sveriges strategi för forskningssamarbete och forskning inom utvecklingssamarbetet där Sida ska arbeta för en ökad förmåga hos samarbetsländer och regionala forskningsaktörer att planera, genomföra och använda forskning i kampen mot fattigdom.
Mål 1: Öka och stärka kvinnor i STLCs deltagande i naturvetenskaplig och teknisk forskning, undervisning och ledarskap. Mål 2: Främja och stärka kvinnliga teknologer och forskare i STLC samarbete och kommunikation med det internationella forskarsamhället och med industrin. Mål 3: Främja erkännande, synlighet och medvetenhet av kvinnors vetenskapliga och tekniska prestationer i STLC. Mål 4: Främja jämställdhet i naturvetenskapliga och tekniska institutioner och organisationer i utvecklingsländerna.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement contribution UNESCO and Sida for OWSD 2022-2026

description.narrative:
The Organization for Women in Science for the Developing World (OWSD) is an international organization founded in 1987 and based at the offices of The World Academy of Sciences (TWAS) in Trieste, Italy. OWSD is a programme unit of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). OWSD is the first international forum to unite eminent women scientists from the developing and developed worlds with the objective of strengthening their role in the development process and promoting their representation in scientific and technological leadership.
The key activities of OWSD include:
- Increasing the participation of women in developing countries in scientific and technological research, teaching and leadership through PhD and early career fellowships;
- Promoting the recognition of the scientific and technological achievements of women scientists in developing countries through awards; and
- Promoting collaboration and communication among women scientists in developing countries and with the international scientific community as a whole through networking activities.
Support from OWSD is in most instances restricted to women scientists from 66 developing countries in which capacity in science and technology is significantly lagging as identified by TWAS (https://twas.org/66-countries). The list includes the 45 least developed countries identified by the United Nations, to which 21 other countries were added because of their low-income levels and specific needs for support in building research capacity.
Sida has supported OWSD since 1998 and is today together with the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation the main funder of OWSD.
Examples of results:
Masters Scholarships for Displaced Women Scientists (WISDOM) programme: The WISDOM programme was lauchend by OWSD in 2023 in partnership with the United Nations Human Rights Council (UNHRC), Hashemite University in Jordan and Istanbul Aydin University in Turkey. The programme expands OWSDs mission to support women in STEM, focusing on displaced women scientists affected by conflict, political instability and natural disasters. These women face significant barriers, including interrupted education and exclusion from professional networks, limiting their contributions to global research and development. The programme aims to address these challenges by partnering with universities, preferably in the Global South, to provide scholarships and capacity-building opportunities for displaced women scientists.
The programme resulted in the award of 10 MSc scholarships at Hashemite University and 14 MSc scholarships at Istanbul Aydin University in 2024 for women coming from Syria (18), Palestine (4) and Afghanistan (2) who have sought refuge in Jordan and Turkey, respectively.
OWSD aims to further expand the WISDOM programme adressing critical needs for displaced women scientists, and in October 2024, the process for identifying a third partner university in Uganda was initiated.
OWSD PhD Fellowship programme: Due to Sida's funding cuts, OWSD did not open any call for PhD fellowships in 2024. Since 1998, OWSD has awarded a total of 576 PhD fellows of which 406 have graduated and 99 are ongoing.
OWSD Membership and National Chapters: OWSD members can meet other members in their own countries and regions through activities organised by OWSD National Chapters. National Chapters exist to support women scientists in and from the Global South with events and activities aimed at promoting women's participation in science and technology, scientific leadership, and scientific decision-making, both at the national and regional levels. National Chapters organise a wide range of activities to achieve these goals, such as training workshops, scientific seminars, outreach to schools, and celebratory events. The number of active OWSD National Chapters grew to 57 in 2024 with new chapters established in Costa Rica, Cuba and Iraq. Sida-funding is not directly used to support the work of National Chapters.
In 2024, OWSD celebrated reaching 10 000 members. This milestone reflects robust growth and a strengthened global outreach. Full and affiliate members totalled to 10,839 and came from 113 countries.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
